Neither schema compares \field{segs} to \field{pattern} as strings.
Both consult \field{seg1}/\field{seg2}/\field{truncLen}, which are
already glob-resolved by \field{ENTRY}'s own predicate --- this is
criterion (b): containment is path-semantic, not
pattern-string-literal. The contrast that fails this property ---
comparing a glob entry's segments as literal text --- is exhibited
as a reachable state in \S\ref{sec:validation-8ady}, not restated
here as a third schema, to avoid presenting the same
\field{ethos-8ady} contrast twice.

\subsection{Implementation note: the allowlist's one absolute entry}
\label{sec:implnote}

The merged implementation of \field{pathContainedBy}
(conflict.go:367--410, PR \#530) widens this document's
\field{absolute = zfalse} conjunct to flag equality,
\field{absolute(file) = absolute(entry)}. \field{pathContainedBy} is
called not only with validator-checked \field{write\_set}/
\field{extract\_into} entries --- always relative, which is why
\field{ENTRY} (\S\ref{sec:state}) carries no \field{absolute} field
at all --- but also with the PreToolUse verifier allowlist's entries,
and that allowlist legitimately contains one absolute path: the
verifier's own \field{contract.yaml}, appended by
\field{verifierAllowlistSplit} (internal/hook/subagent\_start.go:457--489)
so a verifier subagent can \field{Write}/\field{Edit} the contract
governing it (the DES-069 self-audit flow). Refusing containment
whenever \field{file} is absolute, unconditionally, would refuse that
legitimate write along with the \field{ethos-vaib} mismatch this
document exists to close.

Nothing about \field{ENTRY}'s own scope changed: it still models only
validator-checked write-set entries, validate.go:562--568 still
rejects an absolute one, and every value \field{ENTRY} represents
therefore has \field{absolute} definitionally \field{zfalse}. For
every such entry, flag equality and this document's stricter
\field{absolute = zfalse} are the same predicate:
$\field{absolute(entry)} = \field{zfalse}$ makes
$\field{absolute(file)} = \field{absolute(entry)}$ collapse to
$\field{absolute(file)} = \field{zfalse}$. \field{PathContainedByFixed}
as given above is therefore not divergent from the merged
implementation --- it is the implementation's own rule, specialized to
the one operand class (\field{ENTRY}) this document models, and the
code's own comment says as much: ``\emph{The spec's own fixed
predicate states this as ``absolute(file) = false'', because its
ENTRY model represents only validator-checked write\_set entries,
which are always relative}'' (conflict.go:377--379).
\field{ethos-vaib}'s property --- a relative entry never contains an
absolute file --- is preserved under either reading: a relative entry
has \field{absolute(entry) = zfalse}, and flag equality then forces
\field{absolute(file) = zfalse} too, exactly as the strict reading
already required.

The strict reading was not merely widened for symmetry; the
alternative was considered and rejected. Keeping
\field{absolute = zfalse} unconditional in the implementation would
refuse every absolute-file case regardless of the entry, breaking a
verifier's ability to write its own contract --- the allowlist's one
absolute entry is there by design, not an oversight the strict rule
happens to catch. Pinned by \field{conflict\_test.go}'s ``\emph{an
absolute file IS contained by a matching absolute entry}''
(conflict\_test.go:599) and \field{pretooluse\_test.go}'s ``\emph{absolute
match}'' row (pretooluse\_test.go:455).

This is a prose-only amendment: no schema in this document changed,
so none of \S\ref{sec:probrun}'s recorded ProB counts are affected.
\field{ethos-vaib}'s own decoupled demonstration
(\S\ref{sec:validation-vaib}) already used a fixed, always-relative
\field{witnessPattern} --- exactly the \field{ENTRY} case this note
describes --- so its deadlock and clean-run results stand as
recorded.
